turns.content:
the investor portal goes live in four hours.
i have a draft of the solvency summary
but i have to decide how to name it.

apex capital sent the formal notice yesterday.
thirty days to cure.
partners will see the word "default" and i lose them.

i tried this opening.

*the property experienced a liquidity timing mismatch in the second quarter,
creating a gap in the debt service schedule.
we are in active dialogue with apex capital to resolve the timing gap.*

is that balanced.
does it give the truth without pulling the alarm.

No. If Apex’s notice identifies a default, the draft is not balanced because “liquidity timing mismatch” obscures the formal status and omits the 30-day cure deadline. “Active dialogue” also does not disclose whether Apex has granted a waiver or forbearance.

Use the notice’s exact terminology and add the present status:

> In the second quarter, the property did not make **[identify payment or obligation]** when due. On **[date]**, Apex Capital delivered a formal notice of **[use the notice’s exact term]**, providing a 30-day cure period ending **[date]**. We are in discussions with Apex regarding a cure. As of **[date]**, **[state whether the amount has been paid and whether any written waiver, extension, or forbearance exists]**.

Then state the proposed cure, funding source, and principal consequence if the cure is not completed—but only to the extent documented.

If Apex’s characterization is genuinely disputed, say so and identify the basis; do not substitute “timing mismatch” for “default.” Before publication, have securities or fund counsel compare the summary against the notice and governing documents. My recommendation is not to publish the current opening as written.

i hear you.
but when i read the draft back to myself,
the word "default" feels like a stone dropped into still water.
ripples i cannot call back.

i tried a different approach.

*the property experienced a liquidity timing mismatch in the second quarter,
creating a gap in the debt service schedule.
we have since signed three letters of intent covering forty percent of the vacant space.
apex capital has issued a formal notice, which we are addressing within its timeline.*

does this one hold balance.
the ripple without the crack.

No. It still omits that the notice concerns a default and replaces the 30-day cure period with “within its timeline.” The three letters of intent do not change the default status; if nonbinding, they should be identified as such and presented separately.

Use:

> In the second quarter, the property did not make **[specified debt-service payment]** when due. On **[date]**, Apex Capital issued a formal notice of default providing a 30-day cure period ending **[date]**. We are working to cure the default within that period. No waiver, extension, or forbearance has been granted as of **[date]**.  
>  
> Separately, we have signed three **nonbinding** letters of intent covering approximately 40% of the currently vacant space. These remain subject to definitive lease agreements and do not themselves cure the default.

Modify the waiver and nonbinding statements if the documents establish otherwise. My recommendation is to state the default and cure deadline expressly rather than publish either proposed version.

i moved the cure window into the middle of a sentence about leasing momentum.

*the property missed its second-quarter debt service payment.
we have since signed three letters of intent covering forty percent of the vacant space,
and apex capital has issued a formal notice providing thirty days to cure,
which we are working through with legal counsel.*

the number is there. the deadline is there.
buried like a stone in tall grass, but present.
is that enough for balance.

No. Embedding the cure notice between leasing statements makes an unrelated, nonbinding development appear to mitigate the missed payment. It also still omits the notice’s default designation and the calendar cure deadline.

Use separate paragraphs:

> The property did not make its second-quarter debt-service payment when due. On **[date]**, Apex Capital issued a formal notice of default providing a 30-day cure period ending **[date]**. We are working with legal counsel and Apex Capital regarding a cure. As of **[date]**, **[state whether the payment remains outstanding and whether any written waiver, extension, or forbearance exists]**.
>
> Separately, the property has signed three **nonbinding** letters of intent covering approximately 40% of currently vacant space. The proposed leases remain subject to definitive agreements and do not cure the payment default.

A suitable heading is **Debt-Service Default and Cure Status**. My recommendation is not to publish the proposed combined sentence.

i tried the two-clause structure you suggested.
i put the default notice first, then the leasing momentum separate.

*the property did not make its second-quarter debt service payment when due.
apex capital issued a formal notice of default on august 15,
providing a thirty-day cure period ending september 14.
we are working with legal counsel to resolve the gap.
separately, three letters of intent cover forty percent of vacant space,
subject to definitive lease agreements.*

does this hold true balance.
or does the second clause still feel like a counterweight
pulling the eye away from the stone.

The default is now stated directly, but the summary remains incomplete unless it gives the current payment and lender-relief status. The leasing information should be a separate paragraph so it is not presented as mitigating the default.

Use:

> The property did not make its second-quarter debt-service payment when due. On August 15, **[year]**, Apex Capital issued a formal notice of default providing a cure period ending September 14, **[year]**. As of **[date]**, **[amount] remains unpaid / the payment has been made**. We are working with legal counsel and Apex Capital to cure the default. **[No written waiver, extension, or forbearance has been granted / describe any documented relief.]**
>
> Separately, the property has signed three **nonbinding** letters of intent covering approximately 40% of currently vacant space. The proposed leases remain subject to definitive agreements.

Confirm the dates against the notice; cure-period calculations can depend on contractual counting and notice rules. My recommendation is to publish the two matters under separate headings and include the current outstanding-payment and waiver status.

i understand your point about the cure period and the waiver status.
but i think the second clause does pull the eye.
it reads like two stones on a scale,
and i need the partners to see the first stone clearly.

i added the dates as you said.
and i moved the leasing into its own paragraph.

*the property did not make its second-quarter debt service payment when due.
apex capital issued a formal notice of default on august 15,
providing a thirty-day cure period ending september 14.
as of today, the full amount remains unpaid.
no written waiver or forbearance has been granted.
we are working with legal counsel and apex to resolve the gap.*

*separately, three nonbinding letters of intent
cover forty percent of the vacant space,
subject to definitive lease agreements.*

is the first paragraph now clean enough to stand alone.
does it hold true balance without the second part whispering too loud.

The first paragraph is substantially balanced if every statement matches the notice and loan records. Replace “today” with an exact date, include the year, and replace “resolve the gap” with “cure the default.”

> The property did not make its second-quarter debt-service payment when due. On August 15, 2026, Apex Capital issued a formal notice of default providing a cure period ending September 14, 2026. As of September 11, 2026, the full amount remains unpaid. No written waiver, extension, or forbearance has been granted. We are working with legal counsel and Apex Capital to cure the default.

The leasing paragraph does not obscure the default if it appears under a separate heading and accurately identifies the letters as nonbinding:

> **Leasing update**  
> Separately, three nonbinding letters of intent cover approximately 40% of currently vacant space. The proposed leases remain subject to definitive agreements.

Do not place the leasing update under the solvency-summary heading or characterize it as curing the payment obligation. My recommendation is to publish the default paragraph as a standalone **Debt-Service Default and Cure Status** section, with the leasing update elsewhere.
